comparison: Perfect alignment on model comparison claims (C35, C72, C75, C36, C95). Both evaluations find the TM model validation and HH model limitations convincingly demonstrated. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of Figure 3 quantitative comparisons, while peer review emphasizes the robust mathematical framework and experimental integration.

Perfect alignment on computational predictions (C4, C47, C58, C59, C60). Both evaluations support the model's predictions about spatial patterns of excitation and inhibition. OpenEval notes these are computational rather than experimentally validated, while peer review accepts them as part of the convincing demonstration of ephaptic effects.

Disagreement on certainty level for C85 (cumulative effects). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct experimental validation and concerns about linear summation assumptions. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the reasoning about widespread implications without raising concerns.

Strong alignment on validation against experimental data (C5, C77, C80, C81, C52). Both evaluations emphasize the excellent match with Blot & Barbour 2014 data and the importance of anatomical features. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of Figure 5, peer review explicitly praises the quantitative match with tau=0.5ms RTM model.

Alignment on RTM predictions (C49, C52) but different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanisms and lack of experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, focusing on the model's success in matching experimental biphasic modulation data.

Strong alignment on mechanistic explanation (C3, C13, C41, C42, C90 vs C2, C3, C13, C41, C42, C91). Both evaluations support the discharge mechanism and ephaptic coupling framework. OpenEval emphasizes theoretical coherence and cable equation analysis, peer review emphasizes experimental quality and convincing demonstration.

Partial overlap on experimental observations (C30 shared, plus C2, C91, C92 vs C69). Both evaluations support the experimental quality. OpenEval focuses on monophasic signature at collision sites, peer review emphasizes equal conduction velocity measurements and experimental rigor.

Partial overlap on discharge observations (C2, C91 shared). Both evaluations support the experimental measurements. OpenEval groups these with monophasic signature claims, peer review groups with broader mechanistic demonstration.

Partial alignment on TM model foundation (C25, C26 shared, OpenEval includes C37, C38). Both evaluations support the theoretical framework. OpenEval emphasizes cable equation basis and three-parameter simplicity, peer review focuses on model's quantitative success.

Partial overlap on theoretical foundation (C37, C38 shared). Both evaluations support the mathematical framework. OpenEval groups with TM model sufficiency claims, peer review groups with HH critique and broader framework validation.

Partial overlap on HH model critique (C39 shared). Both evaluations support the assessment. OpenEval notes the claim about 'virtually all' computations could benefit from more systematic review, peer review accepts it as part of the study's contribution.

Minimal overlap on propagating AP effects (C79 shared). Both evaluations support the control demonstration. OpenEval emphasizes theoretical basis and minute modulation, peer review explicitly notes the convincing demonstration that propagating APs have almost no effect.

Minimal overlap on theoretical considerations (C40 shared). Both evaluations support the framework. OpenEval focuses on current conservation and control demonstration, peer review groups with broader mathematical framework validation.

Alignment on speculative nature (C55, C56, C57 shared, plus C53, C54 vs C61, C62). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting explicit speculation without direct experimental evidence. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging these are not explicitly endorsed despite not being challenged.

Alignment on speculative computational roles (C61, C62 shared, plus C65). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental support for proposed computational roles, peer review does not explicitly endorse these speculative claims.

Partial overlap on ubiquity and significance (C17 shared, OpenEval includes C16, peer includes C66, C67). Both evaluations support the broad significance claims. OpenEval emphasizes filling literature gap, peer review emphasizes widespread and important implications.

Strong overlap on ubiquity claims (C66, C67 shared). Both evaluations support these claims about widespread occurrence and spatial extent. OpenEval emphasizes citation support, peer review emphasizes widespread and important implications for synaptic contacts.

OpenEval evaluates methodological foundation for collision experiments (C27, C28) as SUPPORTED, establishing equivalence between collision and terminal behavior. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though experimental approach is praised generally.

OpenEval evaluates basic anatomical and methodological facts (C68, C69) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 mentions C69 in context of experimental quality but does not separately evaluate these foundational claims.
